I couldn't write these notes. None of the source pages loaded, so I have nothing I'm allowed to report.

My first attempt to fetch the pages crashed because my code didn't handle the format the fetch tool returned. When I tried again, I had run out of tool uses for this turn. As a result, I didn't read a single page from any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say, cite a URL for every point and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. Under those rules I can't give you any notes on Psalm 111, by verse or otherwise. Anything I wrote now would come from memory, not from sources.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start by retrieving these pages:

- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-111/, plus the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Barnes commentaries on biblehub.com (psalms/111.htm), and Precept Austin's Psalm 111 page.
- **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on Psalm 111 (spurgeon.org or studylight.org), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), and relevant pages on Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY and the LCMS. I'd especially look for whether they differ on v. 10, "the fear of the LORD," and on v. 9, "redemption" and "covenant."
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on Psalm 111 (netbible.org), including the poem's acrostic structure, and Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org. Augustine uses the Greek Old Testament's numbering, so this psalm appears there as Psalm 110, at /fathers/1801110.htm.

Sorry for the wasted turn. If you send the request again, I'll fix the code first.
